title: cross-team-engineering-leadership-weekly-staff-notes-2026-04-20
content:
Date: 2026-04-20
Facilitator: Evelyn Zhang
Duration: 60 minutes
Location: Zoom / #eng-leadership

AGENDA:
- Quick wins & shout-outs (5m)
- Cross-team status updates (30m): serving-runtime, infra, observability, private-deployments, console
- Open blockers & escalation (10m)
- Decisions and roll-forward plan for next week (10m)

NOTES / DISCUSSION:
1) Quick wins & shout-outs
- Shout-out to Samir and infra team: completed the new GPU node SKU rollout in us-west-2 with zero customer incidents.
- Claire: new observability dashboard for token-level latency is live in staging and already surfaced a regression for a canary model — nice catch.

2) Team updates (concise):
- Serving Runtime (Samir)
  - Progress: Canary for continuous-batching optimization (PR #824) passed internal perf tests: 12–18% throughput improvement at median sequence lengths. Canary will be promoted to canary-1 route tomorrow.
  - Risk/blocker: Memory fragmentation observed under long-lived KV workloads (multi-client, >60k active sessions). Root cause investigation ongoing (SERV-2897).
  - Next steps: Add additional end-to-end load test scenarios; plan targeted GC / allocator tweak next week.

- Infrastructure (Aisha)
  - Progress: GPU SKU rollout done (us-west-2), next - us-east-1 scheduled Thu 4/22. Autoscaling tuning continues for Dedicated clusters.
  - Blocker: Cloud provider quota increase for burst nodes delayed; working with account team to expedite (INFRA-201). Impact: short-term reduced burst capacity for a high-throughput customer.

- Observability (Claire)
  - Progress: Token-level latency dashboard in staging; delta alerts configured for 95th pct changes. Started recording per-route cost breakdowns.
  - Blocker: Metric cardinality growth when sampling per-customer traces; exploring aggregation window adjustments (OBS-412).
  - Note: Will coordinate with Serving Runtime to add lightweight tracing hooks to reduce trace size.

- Private Deployments (Miguel)
  - Progress: On-prem installer RC candidate shipped to 2 pilot customers; initial install feedback positive.
  - Blocker: KMS integration for one customer discovered key rotation bug — patch scheduled for 4/23.

- Console / Rollouts (Jon)
  - Progress: Rollout UI for canary/A-B experiments is now in internal beta with Product; supports automated fallback policy configuration.
  - Blocker: UX copy and multi-tenant permission edge cases need sign-off from security team.

3) Cross-team blockers & escalations
- Memory fragmentation (SERV-2897) flagged as priority P1. ACTION: serving-runtime + observability to collaborate on reproducer and profiling timeline.
- Quota increase (INFRA-201) may limit burst capacity for next week. ACTION: infra to prepare contingency routing policy to shift lower-priority traffic to cheaper model variants temporarily.
- Metric cardinality (OBS-412) needs a resolution before we enable token-level retention for all customers; possible interim solution is sampled retention per customer tier.

4) Decisions
- Promote continuous-batching canary (PR #824) to canary-1 route on 4/21 after additional smoke tests. If no regressions in 48 hours, schedule roll to 50% traffic on 4/24. (Decision by consensus)
- For infra quota delays, approve temporary routing policy to fall back to compatible quantized model variant for overflow. A/B to measure impact on latency and quality.

5) Action items (owner — due date)
- Samir + Claire: produce minimal reproducer for KV cache fragmentation; include heap profile and trace sample. Due: 2026-04-22. Linked: SERV-2897.
- Aisha: escalate quota request with cloud account team and provide contingency runbook. Due: 2026-04-21. Linked: INFRA-201.
- Miguel: ship KMS key-rotation patch and coordinate revalidation with pilot customer. Due: 2026-04-23.
- Jon + Product: finalize rollout UI permission model and UX copy; run security review. Due: 2026-04-27.
- Claire: propose sampling/aggregation config for token-level observability to limit cardinality. Due: 2026-04-24.
- Evelyn: draft customer-facing note template in case the quota issue impacts SLAs; coordinate with CS. Due: 2026-04-21.

6) Risks / Notes for Execs
- If memory fragmentation persists, it could increase tail latency for long-lived workloads and require a short maintenance window to roll allocator fixes. Plan and customer comms needed.
- Quota delays are the most likely near-term operational risk; expecting mitigation via routing policy but will monitor closely.

7) Parking lot / follow-ups
- Longer-term: evaluate allocator redesign vs. incremental mitigations for KV cache fragmentation (tech-debt spike proposal for Q3).
- Observability: plan for controlled token-level retention for enterprise customers as paid add-on.

NEXT MEETING: 2026-04-27, same time. Agenda to include: fragmentation findings, quota escalation outcome, and canary metrics for continuous-batching promotion.

Document owner: Evelyn Zhang
Minutes prepared by: Evelyn Zhang (notes are working draft; please add comments in the doc and link any follow-up tickets).
